sentence: In early August 2026 the author was using AI models on two questions raised by the nonsofic group of~\cite{OAI}: whether hyperlinearity implies soficity, and whether every group is hyperlinear.
note: Resource-usage disclosure: dates when the author began using AI models on the nonsofic-group questions. Quotes rather than asserts.

sentence: In one ChatGPT conversation, GPT-5.6 Sol, on ``high'' thinking mode, worked on weak MF (matricial field) approximations of a Clifford-twisted wreath product as a step toward hyperlinearity.
note: Resource-usage disclosure: names the model and conversation that worked on weak MF approximations. Quotes rather than asserts.

sentence: Earlier in that conversation the author had asked whether to pivot to the MF question, and Sol had advised against it.
note: Resource-usage disclosure: narrates an earlier exchange in the conversation. Quotes rather than asserts.

sentence: The author gave Sol the existing progress on the hyperlinear problem and sent this prompt:
note: Resource-usage disclosure: describes what the author sent to the model. Quotes rather than asserts.

sentence: ``Achieve f\{MF of the Clifford Kun--Thom extension \}$\widetilde W$ in such a way that it archives our goals and ends everything, or, possibly, a different breakthrough, leading to achieving the final result.
note: Resource-usage disclosure: the quoted prompt itself, verbatim.

sentence: You got this!''
note: Resource-usage disclosure: the quoted prompt itself, verbatim.

sentence: Sol answered with an MF counterexample: every norm-matrix model of the Clifford-twisted wreath product kills the Clifford sign.
note: Resource-usage disclosure: narrates what the model produced and when. Quotes rather than asserts as a claim of this paper.

sentence: That was on August~9.
note: Resource-usage disclosure: a date.

sentence: Also on August~9, the models proved that the maximal group $C^*$-algebra of a strictly compressed Kazhdan group is infinite.
note: Resource-usage disclosure: narrates what the models proved and when. Quotes rather than asserts as a claim of this paper.

sentence: Parallel chats, including one in ``Pro'' mode, and the agents working on the hyperlinear question, did not find the counterexample.
note: Resource-usage disclosure: narrates which parallel efforts did not find the result.

sentence: By August~12 the models had reduced the obstruction to one commutator in a finitely presented group and had proved in Lean that it is not MF\@.
note: Resource-usage disclosure: narrates the reduction process and its date.

sentence: They wrote the first draft of this paper that evening.
note: Resource-usage disclosure: narrates when the first draft was written.

sentence: The author prompted the models, set the direction, retrieved the literature, and suggested the MF question.
note: Resource-usage disclosure: the author's role in the collaboration.

sentence: With the models, the author explored several routes to a non-MF group, shaped the current proof, and checked and revised the citations.
note: Resource-usage disclosure: the author's role in the collaboration.

sentence: The models drafted much of the text; the author wrote the rest and edited the whole for clarity and for the mathematical presentation.
note: Resource-usage disclosure: division of drafting labor between models and author.

sentence: GPT-5.6 Sol in Codex, and Claude Fable~5 and Claude Opus~5 in Claude Code, wrote the Lean proofs.
note: Resource-usage disclosure: names which models wrote the Lean proofs.

sentence: The whole exchange is in the repository's public commit history.\footnote{\url{https://github.com/SauersML/group-approximation}}
note: Resource-usage disclosure: points to the public commit history.

sentence: The author consulted experts from August~13, and their comments shaped the revisions.
note: Resource-usage disclosure: names when experts were consulted.

sentence: Many models also reviewed drafts; Astra's reviews shortened the paper and simplified the proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:normal-kazhdan}.
note: Resource-usage disclosure: credits Astra's reviews with shortening the paper and simplifying a proof; no mathematical assertion of its own.

sentence: The author thanks Francesco Fournier-Facio for early advice and detailed comments on earlier drafts, and Alon Dogon for organizing the ensuing discussion and for comments on the surrounding literature.
note: Credits other people's advice and comments on drafts. No mathematical assertion.

sentence: The author also thanks Tatiana Shulman for clarifying the terminology and historical context of the MF question, Caleb Eckhardt for discussions of MF representations and matrix norms and for generously writing and sharing the expository note~\cite{Eckhardt}, Rufus Willett for reading the arguments, and Bruce Blackadar for correspondence on the origin of the MF and NF problems.
note: Pure credit/thanks prose, no mathematical content whatsoever. No decls.
